note: Virtual threads: buffered (SYNC / DIRECT heap fallback / VesperaClient.send) dispatches from a virtual thread now poll the Rust dispatch once on the calling thread (new JNI symbol AsyncDispatch.dispatchPollFirst0) and only park on a Tokio-completed CompletableFuture when the handler has to wait. A handler that completes without waiting no longer pays the two cross-thread wake-ups of dispatchAsync + join(): on the rust-jni-demo /health GET (24 CPUs, JDK 21) single-caller p50 drops from 15.5 us to 1.3 us and throughput at 64-1000 virtual threads rises ~5x (1.2M -> 6.1M ops/s), while waiting handlers still release the carrier (no pinning across I/O). -Dvespera.virtualThread.pollFirst=false restores the previous always-park behaviour. The bridge JAR and cdylib must come from the same release (new native symbol).
